title: Restriction and insertion as a natural chain map on strict systems
statement:
Fix $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, its algebraic closure $k$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $R$, a uniformizer $\varpi$, and $A_n=R/\varpi^n$, $n\ge1$ [def-trf-coefficient-conventions]. Put $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$ and let $g:s\to s$ be any scheme automorphism [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. On the small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] put $B_n=(A_n)_s$, with reductions $\rho_n:B_{n+1}\to B_n$, and $\widehat R_s=\lim_nB_n$, with projections $\pi_n$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Let $F=g^{-1}$, with actions transported by $c_n^{-1}$ for the canonical coefficient isomorphisms $c_n:FB_n\to B_n$ [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison]. Let $\mathscr S_s$ be the strict system category: its objects are $B_n$-module sheaves $M_n$ and quotient-linear maps $v_n:M_{n+1}\to\operatorname{Res}_{\rho_n}M_n$, and morphisms are component maps commuting with $v_n$ [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. Let $G$ apply $F$ at each level, retaining the transported transitions. Let $\Gamma_\bullet$ mean levelwise sections restricted along $R\to A_n$, with all original transitions retained, valued in $\operatorname{Tow}(\operatorname{Mod}R)$ [def-trf-coefficient-tower-operations], the indexing $n\geq1$ here being identified with the $\mathbb N$ indexing there (where $A_i=R/\varpi^{i+1}$) by $n=i+1$. Use unbounded cochain complexes [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

Put $U=(s\xrightarrow{\mathrm{id}}s)$ and $V=(s\xrightarrow g s)$. For each degree $i$ and level $n$, define $\sigma^g_{M_n^i}:M_n^i(U)\to(FM_n^i)(U)$ by restriction along $g:V\to U$, followed by the inverse-image colimit insertion at $(V,(\mathrm{id},\mathrm{id}))$ and sheafification, exactly as in [lem-weil-point-automorphism-restriction-natural]. Under the site-reindexing identification $(FM_n^i)(U)\cong M_n^i(V)$ the insertion is identity. These components are $A_n$-linear for the specified target action and satisfy the strict transition identity
$$\Gamma(Fv_n)\sigma^g_{M_{n+1}}=\sigma^g_{M_n}\Gamma(v_n).$$
There is a unique natural $R$-linear chain map of whole strict towers
$$u^g_M:\Gamma_\bullet M\longrightarrow\Gamma_\bullet GM$$
with these degreewise and levelwise components. For every system chain map $f:M\to M'$ it satisfies
$$\Gamma_\bullet(Gf)u^g_M=u^g_{M'}\Gamma_\bullet(f).$$
This asserts strict commutation before localization, for arbitrary quotient-linear transitions, rather than only for transitions obtained by reduction of a single complex. No cartesianness, boundedness, constructibility, finite Tor-amplitude or derived-completeness hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: For every $i,n$, apply [lem-weil-point-automorphism-restriction-natural] with $\Lambda=A_n$ to $M_n^i$. It gives exactly the specified restriction followed by insertion and sheafification, identifies insertion with identity in $(FM_n^i)(U)\cong M_n^i(V)$, and gives $\sigma(bx)=c_n^{-1}(b)\sigma(x)$. The prescribed target action therefore makes this component $A_n$-linear, hence $R$-linear through $R\to A_n$.

proof.text: The coefficient compatibility of [lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image](3) applied to $A_{n+1}\to A_n$ gives $\rho_n c_{n+1}=c_nF\rho_n$, hence $F\rho_n c_{n+1}^{-1}=c_n^{-1}\rho_n$. Thus transporting $Fv_n$ gives a quotient-linear transition with precisely the prescribed target action. Restriction of scalars changes neither sections nor restrictions [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]; after restricting to $R$, all transitions are $R$-linear.

proof.text: Fix $i,n$ and $x\in M_{n+1}^i(U)$. In the reindexing coordinates of [lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image](1), $\Gamma(Fv_n)\sigma(x)=v_n(V)(x|_V)=v_n(U)(x)|_V=\sigma\Gamma(v_n)(x)$. The middle equality is naturality of the underlying sheaf morphism $v_n:M_{n+1}^i\to\operatorname{Res}_{\rho_n}M_n^i$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. This proves the strict transition identity for arbitrary $v_n$, without expressing it as reduction of a single object.

proof.text: The preceding section restrictions define a natural transformation of whole R-module towers in the concrete ringed sequence-site presentation [def-coef-ringed-sequence-site]. At every level, transition naturality is the functoriality of restrictions; naturality in a module map is its underlying presheaf naturality [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Identify the explicit restriction functor with the specified coefficientSequenceRestriction using its uniqueness characterization. Both sections and transported inverse image preserve addition. Apply Mathlib NatTrans.mapHomologicalComplex to obtain the natural chain map on arbitrary unbounded complexes [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. The component formula is preserved by transport along the restriction-functor equality. Any two transformations with the prescribed components agree at every object, degree, and tower index, so extensionality proves uniqueness. No derived semilinear-calculus theorem is used.
